title: "Understanding Unix Signals"
---

# Understanding Unix Signals

Signals are asynchronous software interrupts sent to a process by the kernel or other processes:

| Signal | Number | Default Action | Description | Catchable? |
|--------|--------|----------------|-------------|------------|
| `SIGHUP` | 1 | Terminate | Terminal hangup or daemon reload | Yes |
| `SIGINT` | 2 | Terminate | Keyboard interrupt (Ctrl+C) | Yes |
| `SIGQUIT`| 3 | Core Dump | Keyboard quit (Ctrl+\) | Yes |
| `SIGKILL`| 9 | Immediate Terminate | Hard kernel uncatchable kill | No |
| `SIGTERM`| 15 | Terminate | Polite request to gracefully terminate | Yes |
| `SIGUSR1`/`SIGUSR2` | 10/12 | Terminate | User-defined custom hooks | Yes |
